classification: Confirmed code defect; runtime impact high-confidence
finding: The program clock advances from requestAnimationFrame wall-clock time even while the current video is waiting, stalled, seeking, or not ready.
impact: The playhead and auxiliary audio can move ahead while picture is frozen, followed by a hard seek or skipped visual material. Editorial timing cannot be trusted.
required_fix: Make media readiness authoritative. Pause the transport clock on waiting/stalled/seeking; resume only after canplay/seeked. Use a shared master clock and explicit buffering state.
acceptance: Under throttled decode/network conditions, the program playhead does not advance during a stall; picture and audio return within one frame at 24 fps.

finding: Every cut remounts a single <video> element keyed by clip ID, with no next-clip preload, double buffer, preroll, or readiness gate.
impact: Cuts can flash black, show the prior frame, or stall on real 4K/AI-generated media and slow disks.
evidence: client/src/components/SequenceEditorWorkspace.tsx — program monitor JSX and currentProgramClip key/src handling
required_fix: Use two alternating video elements or a media buffer, preload the next source, seek it before the seam, and swap only after readiness is acknowledged.
acceptance: A 50-cut mixed-codec sequence plays three consecutive passes with zero black frames, zero stale frames, and no seam stall.

finding: Preview gain converts dB to linear gain and clamps it to 0–1, while the editor/export path permits positive gain up to +12 dB.
impact: Preview and export do not match. A +12 dB clip previews at unity but exports at roughly 3.98× linear gain, creating surprise loudness or clipping.
evidence: client/src/components/SequenceEditorWorkspace.tsx — dB gain clamp; server/ffmpeg.js — export volume application
required_fix: Use Web Audio GainNode or another path that supports gain above unity, or remove positive gain from the UI/export contract.
acceptance: For -24, -12, 0, +6, and +12 dB, preview and exported integrated/peak levels agree within 0.5 dB.

finding: Per-file import failures are swallowed, and completion messaging reports only the imported count without a failed/rejected count, reason list, or retry.
impact: Users can believe a folder was handled successfully while assets are missing. This is especially dangerous in large production drops.
evidence: client/src/components/SequenceEditorWorkspace.tsx — importDroppedMedia per-file empty catch and summary notice
required_fix: Return a structured result for every file: imported, duplicate, unsupported, oversized, failed. Present a persistent summary and retryable failure list.
acceptance: A mixed 20-file drop reports scanned/imported/skipped/failed totals that add up exactly to 20, with reason and retry for each failure.

finding: The client accepts image extensions but never categorizes/imports them, and accepts AVI while the server rejects AVI.
impact: Images disappear silently and AVI produces a hidden failure. The drop-zone promise is not truthful.
evidence: client/src/components/SequenceEditorWorkspace.tsx — extension allowlist/classification; server/sequence-editor.js — server extension validation
required_fix: Create one shared media-type contract. Import images into a defined bin/workflow or reject them visibly. Align AVI support on both layers.
acceptance: Every advertised extension has an end-to-end test and a visible deterministic result; no accepted file vanishes silently.

finding: Large uploads use in-memory multipart buffering and synchronous disk writes, with very large configured limits.
impact: Large AI-video imports can spike process memory, block the event loop, freeze the UI/API, or terminate the server.
evidence: server/index.js — multer memory storage/limits and import routes; server/sequence-editor.js — synchronous writes
required_fix: Stream multipart data directly to a staging file, validate while streaming, atomically rename, expose progress, and make limits explicit in the UI.
acceptance: Importing files near the configured limit does not cause a material event-loop stall or memory spike proportional to full file size.

finding: Latest/segment filtering was removed from the visible controls, its remaining branch is a no-op, and the default filter changed from Active to All.
impact: The take bin becomes noisier and the fastest segment-review path disappears in the very commit advertised as improving takes.
evidence: client/src/components/SequenceEditorWorkspace.tsx at parent 680f18c versus 17234f7 — takeFilter state, visibleMedia filter, rendered filter buttons
required_fix: Restore Active, Latest/segment, and All; default to Active; add regression tests for item membership and default state.
acceptance: Latest/segment shows only the newest eligible take for the selected segment, Active remains default, and All is an explicit opt-in.

finding: The picker can display a selected workflow before that graph has been loaded into the iframe, and success is announced without a bridge acknowledgement that the graph actually loaded.
impact: The label and canvas can disagree. A user can edit or queue the wrong graph while believing the selected workflow is active.
evidence: client/src/components/ComfyUIWorkspace.tsx — initial picker state, loadWorkflow/injectGraph, URL fallback and success notice
required_fix: Separate selected, loading, and loadedWorkflow IDs. Auto-load deliberately or show 'not loaded'. Require an explicit iframe bridge ACK containing workflow ID/hash before success.
acceptance: The toolbar never claims workflow X is loaded unless the iframe returns an ACK for X; initial state is unambiguous.

finding: Rapid workflow changes are not cancellation- or sequence-token-protected, and loading another workflow does not confirm unsaved graph edits.
impact: An older request can overwrite a newer selection, and local graph work can be destroyed without warning.
evidence: client/src/components/ComfyUIWorkspace.tsx — loadWorkflow request lifecycle and option change handling
required_fix: Abort or ignore stale loads, serialize bridge application, track canvas dirty state, and require discard/save confirmation.
acceptance: In a 20-change rapid-selection test, only the final workflow loads. Modified graphs cannot be replaced without an explicit user decision.

finding: The server scans BlokeyUI/ComfyUI/user/default/workflows, but BlokeyUI explicitly ignores **/user/default/workflows/ and those local workflow files were not committed.
impact: 17234f7 alone cannot reproduce the developer's picker inventory. Clean machines can show a partial/empty library or resolve different graphs.
evidence: server/aaa-workflow.js — WORKFLOW_ROOT; root .gitmodules; BlokeyUI .gitignore; pinned BlokeyUI tree
required_fix: Package supported workflow JSON in a tracked product directory with a manifest/version/hash, or provide a deterministic installer/import step and a first-run missing-library state.
acceptance: A clean recursive clone produces the same supported picker inventory and graph hashes as the release machine, or clearly blocks with actionable setup.

finding: No behavioral browser tests cover play, cuts, takes, folder drop, or the Comfy picker; the commit has no CI status/workflow run, and main/master have no required checks.
impact: The primary advertised workflows can regress while both release branches still accept the commit.
evidence: tests/sequence-editor-ui.test.mjs; tests/e2e/uat-harness.mjs; tests/e2e/uat-p0.browser.mjs; package.json; branch/status metadata
required_fix: Add real Playwright browser tests, API contract tests, accessibility checks, and required branch protection on one canonical release branch.
acceptance: The P1 acceptance cases run in CI and must pass before merge; main and master cannot advance without the required checks.

finding: No visible buffering, waiting, stalled, seeking, or decode-error state exists in the program monitor.
impact: Users cannot distinguish a paused transport, a broken source, and a temporary media stall.
required_fix: Add a clear state overlay and retry/relink action.
acceptance: Each media state has distinct text/icon treatment and screen-reader announcement.

finding: HTMLMediaElement.play() rejections and auxiliary-audio playback errors are swallowed or reduced to silently stopping playback.
impact: Autoplay/device/codec errors appear as random transport failure.
required_fix: Surface actionable errors with source/track context.
acceptance: A forced play rejection produces a persistent error and recovery path.

finding: Program video and auxiliary audio use separate HTMLMediaElement clocks with relatively loose correction thresholds.
impact: Dialogue and effects can audibly drift before correction; corrections can be discontinuous.
required_fix: Use one master audio clock and schedule sources against it.
acceptance: A 10-minute mixed timeline remains within 20 ms A/V drift.

finding: Audio fades are updated from requestAnimationFrame and will be throttled in background/occluded tabs.
impact: Fades can become stepped, delayed, or jump to the wrong level.
required_fix: Schedule gain automation on an audio clock.
acceptance: Fade envelopes remain correct after tab backgrounding and restoration.

finding: There is no master meter, clip meter, clipping indication, or preview master gain.
impact: Users cannot detect overloads or judge loudness before export.
required_fix: Add peak/RMS or LUFS-oriented metering and a clipping indicator.
acceptance: Positive-gain clipping is visibly identified during preview.

finding: HTMLMediaElement seeking is not frame-accurate for long-GOP sources, but the UI presents frame/timeline precision.
impact: Trim and cut review can show a nearby keyframe rather than the intended frame.
evidence: Sequence editor direct source seeking architecture
required_fix: Use proxy/intraframe media or frame-serving for editorial review, and label precision limits.
acceptance: A frame-index fixture lands on the expected frame at each tested cut.

finding: Track play controls visually mirror global program playback rather than clearly representing lane-specific audition state.
impact: Users cannot tell what will play or which control owns transport.
required_fix: Separate program transport from solo/audition controls and label both.
acceptance: Control state remains unambiguous in mute, solo, locked, and program-play combinations.

finding: No explicit cut-preroll or seam-readiness logic is present.
impact: The viewer discovers decode latency at the cut rather than before it.
required_fix: Prepare the next source before the seam and expose a degraded-preview mode when impossible.
acceptance: Cut readiness is established before the seam for supported media.

finding: Changing a filter can leave the source monitor showing an item no longer visible in the bin.
impact: Selection and visible collection disagree.
evidence: selectedMedia derives from all media while visibleMedia is filtered
required_fix: Clear, preserve with an explicit hidden-selection banner, or reveal the selected item.
acceptance: A hidden selection is never presented as though it belongs to the current filtered set.

finding: The media/take list renders without virtualization.
impact: Large takes libraries and repeated folder imports can make scrolling and interaction sluggish.
required_fix: Virtualize rows and stabilize item keys/heights.
acceptance: A 10,000-item fixture scrolls and filters responsively.

finding: Retry-all starts multiple probes while sharing one global probing boolean; the first completion can clear busy state while others remain active.
impact: The UI can enable conflicting actions and falsely appear finished.
required_fix: Track a set/count of active probes and aggregate result state.
acceptance: Busy state remains true until the final concurrent probe settles.

finding: Failed auto-probes are retained in a ref and are not automatically retried during the same mount.
impact: Transient probe failures remain stale until manual intervention or remount.
required_fix: Use bounded retry/backoff and expose failure state.
acceptance: A transient first failure retries deterministically and settles visibly.

finding: There is no direct, explicit 'Replace selected timeline clip with selected take' action.
impact: A common editorial task requires indirect context and is easy to perform against the wrong target.
evidence: Sequence editor take and timeline action surface
required_fix: Add a primary replace action with target segment/timeline confirmation.
acceptance: One keyboard-accessible action swaps the selected clip and preserves trim policy predictably.

finding: No previous/next take cycling, A/B compare, side-by-side compare, or keyboard audition exists.
impact: Reviewing many generations is slow and cognitively expensive.
required_fix: Add segment-scoped cycling and compare modes.
acceptance: A reviewer can audition all takes for one segment without moving pointer focus.

finding: When a segment is scoped, media with no segment ID can remain visible.
impact: Unregistered folder imports pollute a segment-focused take review.
required_fix: Make unassigned media an explicit separate group/filter.
acceptance: Segment scope contains only that segment unless 'Include unassigned' is enabled.

finding: Active/Latest status is conveyed with very small badges and weak hierarchy.
impact: Status is hard to scan and easy to misread.
evidence: Sequence editor media card badge rendering
required_fix: Use larger labeled state chips and selected-target linkage.
acceptance: Status is legible at 100%, 125%, and 150% scaling.

finding: Take filter choice is not persisted per user/project.
impact: Users repeatedly restore their preferred review mode.
required_fix: Persist a project/user preference with a safe default.
acceptance: The chosen filter restores after navigation and relaunch.

finding: Folder traversal can be lengthy, but upload/busy state starts only after traversal completes.
impact: A deep folder appears to do nothing after drop.
required_fix: Show scanning state immediately with discovered/eligible counts.
acceptance: Feedback appears within 100 ms of drop and updates throughout traversal.

finding: Uploads are sequential with no per-file progress, total progress, current filename, pause, or cancel.
impact: Large imports feel frozen and cannot be safely interrupted.
required_fix: Add bounded concurrency, progress, and cancellation.
acceptance: A 100-file import exposes deterministic progress and can cancel without corrupting metadata.

finding: If any DataTransfer item yields a webkit entry, fallback files are not added; mixed payloads can lose non-entry items.
impact: Some dragged files disappear from mixed operating-system/browser payloads.
required_fix: Merge and de-duplicate both entry traversal and dataTransfer.files.
acceptance: Mixed file/folder payload fixtures import every eligible file exactly once.

finding: Folder traversal relies on nonstandard webkitGetAsEntry without a tested standards-based fallback.
impact: Behavior can differ across Chromium, Firefox, and future browser versions.
required_fix: Provide feature detection, fallback input picker, and explicit unsupported-browser guidance.
acceptance: Supported-browser matrix has passing folder and multi-file import cases.

finding: Dropping media onto the timeline imports it to the bin rather than inserting it at the drop time/track.
impact: The drop target visually promises an edit operation but performs a library operation.
evidence: Timeline onDrop wired to folder/media import
required_fix: Either insert at the drop location or restrict import drop affordance to the bin and label it.
acceptance: The result matches the visible drop target and preview indicator.

finding: Relative folder hierarchy is discarded.
impact: Production organization, scene/take grouping, and provenance are lost.
evidence: Import payload stores flattened file metadata
required_fix: Preserve normalized relativePath and optionally mirror bins/folders.
acceptance: Nested folder structure is recoverable from imported metadata.

finding: Repeated drops create new copies without hash/size/path duplicate detection.
impact: Disk and bins balloon; users cannot tell which duplicate is canonical.
evidence: Import server copy behavior and client messaging
required_fix: Preflight duplicates and offer skip, link existing, or copy.
acceptance: Re-dropping an identical folder produces a clear duplicate decision rather than silent copies.

finding: Import resets media-tab/filter context to All.
impact: Users lose their segment/take review context after every drop.
required_fix: Preserve context and offer 'Show imported'.
acceptance: Import does not change the active filter unless the user chooses to reveal new assets.

finding: Newly imported media is not automatically selected or grouped as a recent import.
impact: Users must search for the result in a potentially large bin.
required_fix: Add a recent-import group and optional selection.
acceptance: The imported set is reachable in one action.

finding: Concurrent import requests update shared document import metadata without an evident revision/lock transaction.
impact: Two simultaneous imports can overwrite each other's document metadata.
required_fix: Use document revision checks or a serialized/atomic update.
acceptance: Parallel imports preserve all entries with no lost updates.

finding: Audio destination naming uses timestamp-based naming without the same collision loop used for video.
impact: Same-name audio uploads in a narrow time window can overwrite.
required_fix: Use UUID/content hash or atomic exclusive creation for every media class.
acceptance: 1,000 concurrent same-name audio imports yield 1,000 distinct files.

finding: A drop containing only unsupported files can return without actionable feedback.
impact: Users do not know whether the drop was seen.
required_fix: Always report scanned and rejected totals/reasons.
acceptance: Unsupported-only drops produce a persistent explanatory result.

finding: There is no failed-only retry or exportable error list.
impact: Users must re-drop entire folders and risk more duplicates.
required_fix: Retain a session result object with retry/export.
acceptance: Retry failed reprocesses only failed items.

finding: Repeated imports can grow both disk copies and imports metadata without cleanup/retention tools.
impact: Projects accumulate difficult-to-manage storage and metadata debt.
required_fix: Add storage usage, duplicate cleanup, and orphan management.
acceptance: Users can identify and safely remove unused imported copies.

finding: Workflow-list responses are parsed as JSON without checking response.ok.
impact: HTTP errors collapse into confusing loading/empty behavior.
required_fix: Validate status and retain per-source error diagnostics.
acceptance: 404/500/invalid JSON each produce source-specific actionable states.

finding: Loading, empty, partial, and error states are not cleanly distinguished; 'Loading workflows…' can persist indefinitely.
impact: Users cannot tell whether to wait, repair setup, or retry.
required_fix: Use an explicit state machine and retry control.
acceptance: Every request terminates in loaded, partial, empty, or error with a next action.

finding: Catalog readiness is captured but options are not disabled when unready.
impact: Users can select workflows known not to be runnable.
required_fix: Disable or clearly mark unavailable entries with remediation.
acceptance: Unavailable workflows cannot produce false load success.

finding: A flat native select is used for a recursive workflow library with no search, grouping, source filter, favorites, or virtualization.
impact: Discovery degrades quickly as the local library grows.
required_fix: Use a searchable command/menu picker grouped by source/category with recent/favorites.
acceptance: A 5,000-workflow fixture can be found by name/path/model in a few keystrokes.

finding: Catalog, local-library, and packaged variants can represent the same logical workflow without clear de-duplication or source identity.
impact: Users can load a different graph than expected and cannot explain machine-to-machine differences.
evidence: Workflow list merge and option labeling
required_fix: Normalize IDs, show source/version/hash, and define deterministic precedence.
acceptance: Every option maps to one visible immutable graph identity.

finding: The server recursively scans the workflow tree and reads graph JSON synchronously on request.
impact: Large local libraries/graphs can block the Node event loop and slow unrelated UI/API activity.
required_fix: Index asynchronously, cache metadata/hash, and invalidate on filesystem changes.
acceptance: Picker list/graph requests do not create observable event-loop stalls on a large library.

finding: Fuzzy substring graph matching can choose an unintended file when IDs overlap.
impact: The wrong workflow can load while the picker label appears correct.
required_fix: Use manifest-backed exact IDs; reject ambiguous matches.
acceptance: Overlapping-name fixtures either resolve exactly or return an explicit ambiguity error.

finding: Some contentWindow/contentDocument accesses occur before the protecting try/catch.
impact: Cross-origin or browser-security errors can escape and prevent fallback/error handling.
required_fix: Move all iframe access inside guarded bridge code and treat cross-origin as a first-class state.
acceptance: A deliberately cross-origin iframe yields a controlled error, not an unhandled exception.

finding: Queueing can scrape iframe DOM text and click a visible Queue control, then report success without job/prompt acknowledgement.
impact: UI changes, localization, or delayed queue failure can create false success.
required_fix: Queue through a versioned API/bridge and return prompt/job ID.
acceptance: Success is shown only after an accepted prompt ID is returned.

finding: embedSrc is initialized from health data but does not clearly resynchronize when the configured Comfy URL changes.
impact: Toolbar status and iframe destination can disagree after restart/reconfiguration.
required_fix: Derive or synchronize iframe source from authoritative health/config state.
acceptance: Changing engine profile updates status and iframe to the same endpoint.

finding: No explicit iframe load timeout, error state, or retry is provided.
impact: A hung engine leaves a blank or indefinite embedded surface.
required_fix: Add timeout, offline/error panel, restart/retry actions, and preserve context.
acceptance: Offline, refused, and hung states each resolve to an actionable panel.

finding: Selecting the already-selected workflow may not force a reload, especially when the fallback URL does not change.
impact: Users cannot recover a modified/broken canvas from the picker.
evidence: Select change and URL fallback behavior
required_fix: Add explicit Reload selected workflow.
acceptance: Reload deterministically restores the selected graph after confirmation.

finding: Changing asset context can preserve any currently valid workflow rather than switching or clearly offering the asset default.
impact: A workflow suitable for the prior asset can remain active for the new one.
required_fix: Show recommended default and prompt to switch when context changes.
acceptance: Context changes cannot silently leave an incompatible workflow presented as appropriate.

finding: defaultForAsset is collected but not surfaced meaningfully in the picker UI.
impact: Users cannot tell which workflow is recommended.
required_fix: Add Recommended badge and reset-to-default action.
acceptance: Recommended workflow is visible and keyboard reachable.

finding: Graph loading depends on private Comfy globals such as app/comfyApp and private methods.
impact: A ComfyUI update can break loading without a compile-time or contract warning.
required_fix: Introduce a versioned extension/bridge owned by Premiere316 with capability negotiation.
acceptance: Unsupported bridge versions fail closed with remediation.

finding: Potentially asynchronous graph-load methods are not awaited before success is shown.
impact: The toolbar can report success while loading later fails.
required_fix: Await bridge completion and handle rejection.
acceptance: Success is emitted only after graph parse, apply, and canvas-ready acknowledgement.

finding: After load, the UI does not prominently show graph source, version/hash, or local-versus-packaged origin.
impact: Reproduction and support are difficult.
required_fix: Show immutable identity and copyable diagnostics.
acceptance: A screenshot/log can identify the exact loaded graph.

finding: Several glyph-only transport/action controls lack robust accessible names and visible tooltips.
impact: Screen-reader and unfamiliar users cannot identify controls.
required_fix: Add accessible names, titles/tooltips, and consistent icon+label semantics.
acceptance: Automated name/role checks pass and a screen reader announces every control distinctly.

finding: Clip reorder and trim handles are pointer-centric with no equivalent keyboard operation or ARIA value semantics.
impact: Keyboard-only users cannot complete core edits.
required_fix: Add keyboard trim/nudge/reorder commands and announce values.
acceptance: The entire edit can be completed without a pointer.

finding: Multiple controls are approximately 16–28 px and fall below comfortable target dimensions.
impact: Mis-click risk rises, especially at high DPI or for motor impairments.
evidence: Sequence editor inline dimensions and Comfy toolbar styles
required_fix: Increase hit areas to at least 40–44 px where practical, without necessarily enlarging the icon.
acceptance: Primary controls meet the project target-size standard.

finding: Important status/context text is rendered around 8–10 px.
impact: Legibility is poor on common Windows scaling and dense production displays.
evidence: Sequence inline styles and Comfy toolbar CSS
required_fix: Raise essential UI text and preserve hierarchy through weight/spacing rather than extreme size reduction.
acceptance: All functional text is readable at 100%, 125%, and 150% scaling.

classification: Confirmed layout constraint; visual impact needs runtime validation
finding: The application and sequence workspace enforce large minimum widths, while dense fixed-height regions are likely to fail on 1366×768/1440×900 and split-screen.
impact: Horizontal overflow, clipped controls, and excessive nested scrolling are likely.
evidence: global styles min-width and SequenceEditorWorkspace minWidth/fixed regions
required_fix: Create responsive density breakpoints and low-height layouts; avoid requiring viewport-wide horizontal scrolling.
acceptance: Core workflows pass at 1366×768, 1440×900, 1920×1080, 4K, and Windows 150% scaling.

finding: Import scanning/progress and playback buffering are not exposed through a consistent live-region status model.
impact: Screen-reader users receive little or no operational feedback.
evidence: Folder import and playback state rendering
required_fix: Add polite progress updates and assertive failure announcements without chatter.
acceptance: A screen reader can follow start, progress, completion, and failure.

finding: Muted small text and dense dark-theme controls appear at risk of insufficient contrast.
impact: Status, metadata, and disabled/enabled distinctions may be hard to perceive.
evidence: Static style review; live color sampling not available
required_fix: Run rendered WCAG contrast checks and adjust semantic tokens.
acceptance: Text and control boundaries meet the chosen WCAG AA targets.

finding: Space/Delete/S shortcuts are global and largely protected only by input-element checks rather than editor focus/context.
impact: Commands can fire while the user is interacting with unrelated non-input controls.
required_fix: Scope shortcuts to an active editor region, support command discovery, and honor modal/contenteditable contexts.
acceptance: No edit command fires outside the focused editor context.

finding: Periodic refresh/filter changes can reorder content without preserving focus or announcing the update.
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users can lose their place.
evidence: Sequence media refresh and list rendering
required_fix: Preserve stable focus/selection and announce meaningful changes.
acceptance: Refresh does not move focus or silently change the active item.

finding: Waveform-like bars are decorative rather than derived from audio.
impact: The UI implies information it does not actually convey.
required_fix: Render real waveform data or use a neutral clip texture.
acceptance: Visual amplitude corresponds to the source or is clearly non-informational.

finding: The feature commit also changes Create Sound, TTS/server areas, and a very large production storyboard file.
impact: Review, rollback, bisecting, and regression attribution are harder.
required_fix: Split product feature, runtime support, and project-data changes into isolated commits/PRs.
acceptance: Each release change is independently reviewable and revertible.

classification: Confirmed evidence gap from user statement
finding: Diagnostics and patch scripts stayed local and are therefore unavailable for review or reproducible repair.
impact: The commit cannot be independently validated against the developer's local evidence/fixes.
evidence: User release note plus absence from changed files
required_fix: Commit sanitized diagnostics, expected outputs, and idempotent patch/migration scripts in a dedicated tooling location.
acceptance: Another machine can reproduce the diagnostic result and repair from source.

finding: The commit is unsigned.
impact: Provenance is weaker than a verified release workflow.
required_fix: Sign protected release commits/tags if provenance is a project requirement.
acceptance: Release tag/commit is verified.

finding: A very large mutable storyboard JSON is included in the same feature commit.
impact: Merge conflicts, repository growth, accidental state rollback, and noisy diffs increase.
required_fix: Move generated/operational project state to appropriate storage or normalize/split it.
acceptance: Feature code review is not dominated by generated production data.

finding: No tests were added for the advertised interactions in this commit.
impact: The new behavior has no regression lock.
required_fix: Land tests with each feature, not as a later patch.
acceptance: Every blocker and primary happy path has an automated regression test.
